description: The figure is a single rendered table (chart_table), two columns wide, with bold-looking serif headers "Species" and "Conditions" separated from the body by a horizontal rule; there are no other grid lines, no axes, no scale bar and no colour. Five specimen rows are listed in reading order: A = "As received", B = "With 15% pre-strain", C = "Heat-treated after 15% pre-strain", D = "Heat-treated after received", E = "Annealed". Every cell is fully legible black text on a white background. The table carries no numeric data column and prints no material designation; the caption supplies the context that these are the conditions of the specimens for the tensile test, that the material is SPCC and that the sheet thickness is 1.2 mm. Its role in the paper is definitional rather than quantitative: it fixes the five condition labels A-E that the other figures use as series names in elastic-modulus and tensile comparisons made before and after plastic deformation, and it records the 15% pre-strain level applied to specimens B and C.

observations.observation: The figure is a two-column table whose column headers are "Species" and "Conditions".
Row A of the table reads Species "A" with condition "As received".
Row B reads Species "B" with condition "With 15% pre-strain".
Row C reads Species "C" with condition "Heat-treated after 15% pre-strain".
Row D reads Species "D" with condition "Heat-treated after received" (wording reproduced as printed, not corrected).
Row E reads Species "E" with condition "Annealed".
The table itself prints no measured property value, no numeric column, no axis and no scale bar; only the pre-strain level 15% appears as text within a condition name.
The specimen labels are single letters A-E; no composition, chemistry or steel grade is printed inside the image.
The caption states that the table gives the conditions of the specimens for the tensile test.
The caption states the material is SPCC with a thickness of 1.2 mm; neither the designation SPCC nor the 1.2 mm thickness is printed inside the image itself.
